deliverables.description: A structured summary documenting the interpreted signal flow, key component locations, relevant electrical specifications, and applicable service procedures extracted from the provided technical documents.

information_nodes.description: Electronic circuit diagram showing component interconnections, node labels, and electrical relationships for the AV equipment under consideration.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Circuit diagrams use schematic symbols, connection lines, and reference designators that require spatial and symbolic interpretation beyond plain text.

information_nodes.description: Function block diagram depicting high-level signal flow and functional relationships among subsystems of the AV equipment.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Block diagrams convey functional stages and signal paths through labeled blocks and directional connectors that require visual interpretation.

information_nodes.description: Technical specifications document listing electrical ratings, input/output parameters, environmental limits, and performance characteristics for the equipment.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Specifications are typically presented as structured text and tabular data listing numerical values and tolerances.

information_nodes.description: Engineering drawing showing physical layout, mounting dimensions, connector positions, and mechanical details of the AV equipment.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Engineering drawings convey dimensional and spatial information through scaled views, callouts, and annotations that require spatial reasoning.

information_nodes.description: Service manual providing troubleshooting procedures, test point locations, disassembly steps, and repair guidance for the AV equipment.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Service manuals combine procedural text with diagnostic flowcharts, test point diagrams, and reference tables.

information_nodes.description: Derived understanding of the end-to-end signal path through the equipment, mapping input stages through processing blocks to output stages.
Derived mapping of key electronic and mechanical components to their physical and schematic locations as shown across the circuit diagram and engineering drawing.
Extracted electrical ratings, tolerances, and signal parameters relevant to installation or repair, consolidated from the specifications and circuit diagram.
Extracted troubleshooting steps, test point references, and repair procedures applicable to the identified equipment and fault context.

Professional assessment that the interpreted signal flow, component layout, electrical values, and service procedures are mutually consistent across all provided documents and sufficient to inform the installation or repair activity.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Schematic symbols, reference designators, interconnection topology, and node labels that define the electrical relationships among components.
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Circuit diagrams encode component identity and connectivity through standardized schematic symbols and line routing that cannot be fully represented in linear text without loss of spatial relationship information.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Functional block labels, signal direction arrows, and inter-block connections that define the high-level signal flow through the equipment.
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Block diagrams represent sequential and parallel signal relationships through spatially arranged blocks and directional connectors, requiring visual interpretation to trace flow.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Physical dimensions, mounting hole positions, connector locations, and spatial relationships among mechanical features of the equipment enclosure.
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Engineering drawings convey scaled geometric and dimensional information that requires spatial reasoning to relate physical features to installation constraints.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Diagnostic flowcharts, test point callouts on board layouts, and disassembly sequence illustrations referenced by the service procedures.
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Service manuals frequently embed decision-flow diagrams and annotated board photographs that guide troubleshooting steps requiring visual reference.

proposed_blueprint.work_objective: Read and interpret a set of AV equipment technical documents—electronic circuit diagrams, function block diagrams, specifications, engineering drawings, and service manuals—to extract the signal flow, component layout, electrical values, and servicing procedures needed to support an installation or repair activity.

deliverables.description: A structured design level document containing defined game mechanics, design guidelines, and mission outlines, written for use by the development team.

information_nodes.description: High-level description of the game's genre, theme, target platform, and intended player experience.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: A text brief is the standard format for communicating the foundational concept and scope of a game project to a designer.

information_nodes.description: Any prior or related design documents, feature lists, or narrative outlines that the new level documentation must align with or extend.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Prior design artifacts may include text specifications and structural diagrams that the designer must reference for consistency.

information_nodes.description: A clear articulation of the core gameplay mechanics—player actions, rules, and systems—that operate within the levels being documented.
Standards and constraints governing level construction, including pacing, difficulty progression, and interaction principles.
Structured descriptions of level missions, including objectives, sequence of events, and success/failure conditions.
Assessment that the defined mechanics and mission structures are consistent with the established design guidelines and the overall game concept.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Structural relationships between game systems, level flow, or mission progression as depicted in prior design artifacts.
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Game design documents frequently use flowcharts or diagrams to represent system interactions and level progression, which the designer must interpret to ensure new documentation is consistent.

proposed_blueprint.work_objective: Develop and maintain design level documentation for a video game, specifying gameplay mechanics, design guidelines, and mission outlines in a structured, reference-ready format.

deliverables.description: A written or revised engineering documentation entry (report section, specification record, or record entry) covering the assigned automotive engineering item, consistent with the existing documentation system.
Documented review findings on the draft or existing documentation, noting discrepancies, gaps, and required corrections with justification.
An entry in the operational records system reflecting the update, its date, its author/owner, and the revision status of the documentation.

information_nodes.description: Statement of which engineering item, subsystem, or document the work covers, and what level of documentation action (write, review, or maintain) is requested.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Scope and request type are normally conveyed as written instructions.

information_nodes.description: The current engineering documentation for the assigned item, including prior revisions, as available in the workspace.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Engineering documentation commonly mixes prose, parameter tables, and embedded schematics or figures that must be read together.

information_nodes.description: The existing records system or log structure used to track documentation status, revisions, and ownership.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Record systems are typically structured as text fields or tables with defined columns and revision identifiers.

information_nodes.description: Underlying engineering data, test results, specifications, or design inputs that the documentation must accurately reflect.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Source engineering data may be numeric tables, marked-up drawings, or plotted results whose values must be transcribed correctly.

information_nodes.description: Internal documentation standards, templates, or formatting and traceability conventions that govern the required documentation form.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Standards and templates are usually textual procedural documents.

information_nodes.description: A consolidated understanding of what the existing documentation currently states about the item, separated into verified content and open gaps.
Item-by-item comparison of documented statements, values, and figures against the technical source material, with discrepancies identified.
Determination of the documentation's revision state, ownership trail, and completeness relative to the records system's required fields.
Judgment on which discrepancies require correction, clarification, or escalation, and which are acceptable, with rationale grounded in the technical source material and documentation purpose.
Conclusion on whether the documentation is fit for internal use after revision review, and what residual limitations internal users should know.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Schematic or layout references embedded in the existing documentation that the text description points to.
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Engineering documentation often embeds schematic figures whose content is not fully restated in prose, so the reviewer may need to interpret the drawing.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Marked-up drawings or plotted test results carrying values that must be transcribed into the documentation.
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Source engineering evidence is frequently supplied as scanned or plotted graphical outputs rather than typed values.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Parameter, revision, and change tables whose row-column structure carries the authoritative values.
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Specification and revision data are commonly organized in tabular form where structure itself conveys meaning.

proposed_blueprint.work_objective: Produce, review, and maintain engineering documentation that accurately records an automotive engineering item's current technical content and history, so internal users can rely on it as an up-to-date record.

deliverables.description: A consolidated project schedule and budget status report for a network project, showing cost and schedule variances, forecast-to-completion figures, and cost-control findings suitable for financial and resource-allocation review.

information_nodes.description: The defined project scope for a network project and its milestone/work-package breakdown that the schedule must represent.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Scope and milestone breakdowns are typically delivered as written project charters or work-breakdown tables; a table is the natural representation for milestone dates and work-package ownership.

information_nodes.description: Planned durations for scheduled network activities and their logical dependencies (which activities must precede others).
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Dependency logic is often recorded in scheduling tables or network-style Gantt/precedence diagrams; the diagram form matters when activity sequencing must be read spatially rather than from a list.

information_nodes.description: The project budget breakdown by cost category (labor, hardware, licensing, services) with planned unit rates or allocations for each line item.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Budget breakdowns are conventionally supplied as line-item tables; tabular form is required to map each cost category to activity and period.

information_nodes.description: Recorded actual expenditures to date and actual completion or earned-progress data for scheduled activities.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Actuals are recorded in time-phased ledgers or progress logs; tables are needed to align cost and progress observations to specific activities and reporting periods.

information_nodes.description: The reporting period end date, currency, and rounding conventions the status report must follow.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Conventions are concise textual parameters typically stated in the task request rather than a document.

information_nodes.description: The time-phased planned value of scheduled work, derived from activity durations, dependencies, and budget line items, expressed by reporting period.
Earned value and actual cost aggregated by reporting period from progress records and actual expenditure data.
Schedule variance and cost variance computed by comparing earned value against planned value and actual cost at the reporting period.
Forecast estimate at completion and estimated completion date derived from current variances and remaining scheduled work.
Identification of critical-path activities and available float, derived from activity durations and dependency logic, that constrains schedule risk.
Judgment on which budget categories or activities are exceeding thresholds, whether variances are material, and which cost-control actions or resource reallocations are warranted.
Recommended schedule and budget adjustments and resource-allocation priorities for financial management review, grounded in the variance and forecast findings.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Activity precedence logic and sequencing as depicted in a Gantt chart or precedence network
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Scheduling deliverables in network engineering are frequently published as Gantt or precedence diagrams; reading the sequencing correctly may require visual interpretation of the chart rather than a text list.

proposed_blueprint.work_objective: Prepare or monitor a network project's schedule, budget, or cost-control system to support financial management and resource allocation decisions for the project.

deliverables.description: A documented determination of the total financial resources required to implement the program, grounded in the compiled accounting records and related data, with the cost build-up and supporting evidence basis stated.
A consolidated summary of the accounting records and related data used, reconciled and organized by cost category and period, identifying the basis for the resource estimate.

information_nodes.description: The underlying accounting records (ledgers, expenditure reports, transaction detail) relevant to program-related costs, as supplied in the workspace.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Accounting records are typically delivered as tabular ledgers or reports and read as structured text/numbers.

information_nodes.description: Other data referenced by the task beyond accounting records (e.g., program characteristics, staffing, or operational inputs) that bears on the resource estimate, as supplied in the workspace.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Program data relevant to resource estimation is typically provided as narrative or tabular records.

information_nodes.description: The definition of the program to be implemented, including what activities or components it comprises, as stated in the task instruction or supplied materials.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Program scope is conveyed in written description.

information_nodes.description: An assessment of which accounting records and related data have been gathered and whether they are complete and sufficient for the estimate, including identified gaps.
Reconciliation and categorization of accounting data into cost categories and time periods aligned with the program's components, eliminating duplication and resolving inconsistencies.
Derived cost rates or per-unit cost bases for the expense drivers implied by the program scope and the categorized records.
The computed financial resources required, built from reconciled cost categories and cost bases applied to the program scope.
A judgment on whether the compiled records are reliable and sufficient to support the resource determination, and what caveats or gaps affect confidence in the result.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Program structure or workflow relationships that inform resource drivers.
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Program operational data may be conveyed as a process or organizational diagram rather than text.

proposed_blueprint.work_objective: Compile the available accounting records and related program data for a proposed program, analyze the aggregated expenditure and resource data, and determine the financial resources required to implement the program, producing a documented resource-requirement determination.

deliverables.description: A structured compliance assessment documenting each reviewed plan, specification, or construction method, identifying specific provisions of applicable codes or regulations, and stating whether compliance is achieved or deficiencies are found.

information_nodes.description: Plans, blueprints, site layouts, or specification documents describing the proposed construction project, including dimensions, materials, structural details, and construction methods.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Blueprints and site layouts are inherently graphical documents conveying spatial relationships, dimensions, and structural details; specifications may also include tabular schedules and textual requirements.

information_nodes.description: Building codes, safety regulations, zoning ordinances, or other legal requirements applicable to the jurisdiction and project type under review.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Codes and regulations are primarily textual legal documents, often supplemented by tabular reference data for dimensions, loads, and material specifications.

information_nodes.description: Contextual information about the project type, occupancy classification, and intended use, which determines which code provisions and safety regulations apply.
information_nodes.modality_rationale: Project scope and classification are communicated through textual descriptions that establish the regulatory framework for the inspection.

information_nodes.description: Specific design parameters, dimensions, materials, structural loads, egress paths, and construction methods extracted from the plans and specifications that are subject to regulatory compliance checks.
Specific provisions, sections, and requirements from applicable codes and regulations that are relevant to the project scope and the extracted design requirements.

For each extracted design requirement, a determination of whether it complies with or violates the corresponding applicable code provision, supported by specific evidence from both the plans and the regulations.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Spatial layout of the building, dimensional relationships between structural elements, egress paths, and placement of safety features as depicted in blueprints or site plans.
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Blueprints and site layouts use graphical conventions to convey spatial and dimensional information that cannot be fully captured in text; interpreting these diagrams is a core professional skill for construction inspectors.

modality_hypotheses.information_needed: Three-dimensional relationships between building systems, clearance distances, and spatial arrangement of structural, mechanical, and life-safety components.
modality_hypotheses.modality_rationale: Site layouts and multi-view blueprints require spatial reasoning to reconcile plan, elevation, and section views into a coherent understanding of the building; this spatial interpretation is essential for verifying compliance with clearance and egress requirements.

proposed_blueprint.work_objective: Review and interpret construction plans, blueprints, site layouts, specifications, or construction methods to determine whether they comply with applicable legal requirements and safety regulations.
